payload.text: THE GUARDS ARE PROVEN ARMED AND DISCRIMINATING AGAINST THE BODIES IN FORCE AS OF 2026-09-22 -- a deliberately narrower sentence than the one this replaces, and than "proven to catch", which the board said until 2026-09-16 and which was wrong then. Re-driven by vc on 2026-09-22, discharging the 2026-08-28 drive's expiry by EXECUTION rather than re-filing it. THE OLD ITEM'S ONE EXCEPTION WAS ALREADY DEAD WHEN IT WAS READ: it said only the header guard's arm predated the drive, and the header guard moved that same day at 84e1ce66f. Last change per body -- whiteboard-clock-guard 2026-09-11, canon-ignore-guard 2026-09-14, append-only-guard 2026-09-19, whiteboard-header-guard 2026-09-22, pre-commit-guards 2026-09-22 -- so ZERO of the six August arms covered a body in force, plus the dispatcher deciding which of them run. The understatement grew while the item sat. THE ROSTER DID NOT GROW BUT ONE SUBJECT MOVED, and that is the find: append-only-guard's second subject changed from `intent/events.jsonl` to `intent/.canon/events/**`. The August drive recorded that subject as its own known hole, in its words -- events.jsonl "exists here at 0 bytes and untracked, so it has no lines to lose and git cannot see it... Untestable rather than untested." Canon events are populated and tracked now and every node commits them daily, so the hole became REACHABLE and nobody re-drove it. SIX ARMS, each staged by explicit pathspec, HEAD as the measurement and rc as corroboration: clock B (stamp with no Z), clock A (future stamp), header (a YAML-escaped value), append-only (.history subject), append-only (CANON subject -- untestable in August), canon-ignore (an ignore reaching canon). All six REFUSED at rc=1 with HEAD unmoved, and restoration was verified rather than assumed -- 0 dirty across all four targets, HEAD unchanged before and after. Self-identification survives: each arm names its own check and quotes the offending value. THE GREEN CONTROL IS REAL RATHER THAN CONSTRUCTED -- six refusals alone are consistent with a gate that refuses everything, and the control is that cc's 68f6872 landed the same day through these exact bodies. A commit that really lands is a better control than a built one, because nothing about it was arranged to pass. RESIDUE, NAMED RATHER THAN GLOSSED: clock check C (an inbox going backwards) is NOT re-driven -- vc stopped because cc had a canon event staged in the shared index and the harness aborts any arm that sees more than its own staged path, so C is outstanding for a reason worth making again. False negatives are untouched, exactly as in August: a fabricated stamp that carries Z, lands in the past and still increases monotonically passes all three clock checks -- a smaller target, not an empty one. Devbin only: the bodies resolve live out of INTENT_HOME, so none of this says whether another estate's carrier reaches them. And the critic gate is a separate leg of the same hook, untested here.
